title: Free and Open Indo-Pacific: A Pillar of Deeper Regional Cooperation
author: IIDA Masafumi
text:
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio meets with Indo-Pacific Quad Foreign Ministers in Manila, Philippines, July 22, 2026.
Credit: U.S. State Department photo by Mateo S. Melendy
In July 2026, the foreign ministers of the Quad countries — Japan, the United States, Australia, and India — met on the sidelines of the ASEAN Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in Manila and issued the “Joint Press Release on Quad Cooperation with ASEAN,” reaffirming their support for ASEAN centrality and unity and the “ASEAN Outlook on the Indo-Pacific (AOIP).” The Quad foreign ministers also reaffirmed their commitment to a “Free and Open Indo-Pacific (FOIP)” and outlined their intention to deepen cooperation with ASEAN, with FOIP as a core pillar.It has been ten years since former Prime Minister Shinzo Abe proposed the FOIP at the Sixth Tokyo International Conference on African Development (TICAD VI) in Nairobi, Kenya, in August 2016. Abe viewed Asia and Africa, and the Pacific and Indian Oceans, as an inseparable and integrated region, and expressed Japan’s determination to maintain “freedom from coercion,” the “rule of law,” and a “market economy” across it. The FOIP philosophy won broad acceptance across the Indo-Pacific, from advanced Western nations such as the United States and Australia to developing countries including African nations, India, and ASEAN member states. In June 2019, ASEAN adopted the AOIP as its own Indo-Pacific vision, guided by principles including ASEAN centrality, inclusiveness, and respect for international law.[...]
